mainEntity.name: What tablet stand works best for classrooms?

acceptedAnswer.text: A classroom tablet stand should hold the screen at a readable angle, stay stable during repeated use, and fit the school device with its case. iBOLT tablet mounts are useful when the setup needs more durability than a consumer stand.

mainEntity.name: Do school tablet mounts need locking hardware?

acceptedAnswer.text: Locking hardware is useful for shared tablets, checkout stations, labs, and high-traffic spaces. It helps prevent device movement, drops, and walk-away risk.

mainEntity.name: Can one tablet mount work across desks, carts, and labs?

acceptedAnswer.text: A modular mounting system can work across multiple locations if the holder, arm, and base are interchangeable. That is why AMPS-compatible or ball-and-socket systems are useful for schools.

mainEntity.name: What makes a school tablet mount better than a consumer stand?

acceptedAnswer.text: School tablet mounts need durability, secure device retention, case compatibility, and repeatable positioning. Consumer stands usually work for light desk use, but they are not built for shared daily handling.
